newsitem.title: USA: US House clears HUD, EPA funding bill for FY' 1997.
newsitem.headline: US House clears HUD, EPA funding bill for FY' 1997.

text.p: The U.S. House late Monday approved a House-Senate compromise bill that includes billions of dollars in funding for federal housing and environmental programs of interest to the municipal bond market.

By a vote of 388-25, the House agreed to provide $64.4 billion in funds for the Department of Housing and Urban Development, Environmental Protection Agency, Veterans Administration and independent agencies.
Earlier in the day, the Senate "deemed" the bill passed upon approved by the House, which means the measure now goes to President Clinton for signature.
The measure includes $3.6 billion for expiring Section 8 housing contracts, below the $4.5 billion cleared recently by the House and $3.8 billion provided by the Senate.
Housing lobbyists, however, said the $3.6 billion apparently is enough to provide HUD the money it needs for renewals of contracts due to expire under the Section 8 rent subsidy program.

The bill cleared last night also provides $4.6 billion for Community Development Block Grants and $1.4 billion for the HOME investment partnerships program, unchanged from totals approved by the House and Senate earlier.
The bill provides $625 million for Clean Water State Revolving Funds and $1.250 billion for Safe Drinking Water State Revolving Funds.
The overall funding measure is three percent higher than Congress appropriated for HUD and the other agencies in the current 1996 fiscal year, but 3.5 percent less than President Clinton requested.
